## Facts and statements

- [statement] Within its firm-performance reporting scope, the GIPS handbook requires returns after transaction costs and permits estimated transaction costs only for portfolios whose actual transaction costs are not known. - [statement] Evidently’s cited drift documentation requires nonempty reference/current columns and filters empty or infinite values for distribution drift. It says default drift tests do not react to increasing empty counts and recommends separate null-share tests.
